messages:
maria.g: Heads-up: Security pushed an egress-hardening change to the prod VPCs ~10m ago, looks like it tightened outbound CIDR to a narrow allowlist. Not sure if allocator metadata service is covered.
kai: saw the alert — lots of GPU node joins stuck in provisioning in aus-southeast-1a and -1b.
andrew: confirm, warm-pool drains started ~5m after the firewall change. Allocation errors show 403 from the metadata-keystore proxy.
maria.g: exact failure snippet from node agent: `ERROR: failed to fetch keystore token: http status 403 from https://keystore.internal/v1/session`
jeff.sre: tagging @security for visibility — is this the intended CIDR lock? :eyes:
ops-bot: Security Change: egress-policy/v2 applied to vpc-prod-llm (by security-runner). Rule summary: outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 -> deny, allow only to {10.0.0.0/16, 52.120.0.0/14}. Rollout: immediate.
maria.g: that allowlist doesn't include the keystore proxy (10.45.128.0/24) — that's the problem.
kai: consequences: allocator can't complete keystore handshake -> node stays NotReady -> autoscaler reduces active GPU pool -> p50 latency rising, token usage spikes for retries -> cost moving to CPU fallback.
andrew: impact metrics: warm-pool size -30% in affected AZs, provisioning latency +600s, failed launch rate ~22%.
jeff.sre: quick options: 1) temporary allowlist keystore CIDR 2) rollback policy 3) whitelist outbound for service tag `keystore` 4) route table NAT workaround. Any preference?
maria.g: prefer minimal blast radius — add the keystore CIDR to allowlist and create a short-lived canary policy for rollout. then follow with a tight audit entry for the change.
kai: agree. please also add a per-AZ exemption for the allocator's subnets: `subnet-llm-*-a,b` to speed recovery.
andrew: I'll open a support ticket to ops to push the allowlist change, and kick a manual warm-pool rebuild once connectivity verified.
jeff.sre: also, audit note: pre-change we didn't have a runbook linking egress CIDR to critical infra services — let's file an action to add service mapping to the egress playbook.
maria.g: filed: ENG-OPS-2245 "egress service registry". assign to kai.
kai: ack. quick checklist I will run once allowlist applied: 1) curl keystore endpoint from a staging node 2) check agent logs for successful token fetch 3) trigger 2 warm-pool joins 4) monitor p50.
ops-bot: Action: Change request opened by andrew - CR#2219. Change window: immediate. Rollback: remove rule by restoring previous ACL JSON.
andrew: applying allowlist now (calling security-runner). ping when live.
security-runner: Change applied. Outbound allowlist updated to include 10.45.128.0/24. Rule id: egress-allow-keystore-2219.
maria.g: can someone run a quick smoke from a stuck tile?
jeff.sre: ran `curl -v https://keystore.internal/v1/ping` from one of the stuck nodes -> HTTP/200, token fetch OK.
kai: warm-pool rebuild started, two nodes reported Ready within 90s. provisioning latency trending down.
andrew: metrics: warm-pool back to -5% delta, failed launch rate <2% now.
maria.g: perfect. postmortem: short outage (~18m) due to missing service CIDR in allowlist after egress-hardening. Root cause: change rollout didn't reference the infra service registry. Remediation: add preflight check to change pipeline that verifies critical CIDRs are covered and raise blocker if not.
jeff.sre: adding retrospective note to the change: please include `keystore` and `allocator` tags in next policy revision. :memo:
ops-bot: Ticket ENG-OPS-2245 updated; owner kai.
maria.g: thanks team. still want a follow-up on cost impact — can finance run a delta of CPU fallback hours and NAT egress charges during the 18m window?
andrew: will ping finance. early estimate: ~0.7k USD due to extra fallback and NAT egress from retries.
jeff.sre: closing thread once we've got finance delta and a pipeline preflight task.
maria.g: closing for now, great rapid response. :thumbsup:
